independent.summary: The test titled 'no log tier prints the matched text' asserts the leak check against an empty-then-refilled buffer: `lines.length = 0` is executed three times inside the try block and the last call is `logSweep(DOMAIN, {}, 12)` at normal tier, so by line 148 `lines` holds only the 'nothing tripped' line. The light and verbose lines — the only ones that could ever carry a match or a scanText preview — were discarded before the assertion, so a regression that printed previews at verbose tier would still pass.

On the rescrape path a finding computed for an unchanged thin page is silently discarded: sweepChunks credits every URL in a rebuilt group chunk's sourceUrls, but only URLs present in pageHashUpdates (changed pages) get scanRules written — unchanged members go through the `unchangedUrls` updateMany, which sets lastScrapedAt only. A thin page that carries a secret and sits in a group rebuilt because a sibling changed is provably flagged this run yet its ScrapedPage row keeps whatever it had (nothing, for any page last crawled before LEO-060), so no chip appears until a full or force scrape.
